messages_1_subject: Finex: follow-up on throughput & latency SLOs
messages_1_body:
Hi Alex / Melissa,

Thanks again for the call today - good to get visibility into the workload. Quick recap of the SLOs and a few clarifying asks so we can size a recommended configuration: 

- Latency targets: you mentioned p95 generation latency target of <= 300ms for short responses (<= 200 tokens) and target p95 of <= 1s for longer streamed responses. Confirm?
- Throughput / traffic shape: need steady-state QPS, peak QPS (burst), and expected request size (tokens per request).
- Concurrency: number of concurrent live sessions/connections during peak.
- Streaming: percentage of requests that will use streaming vs full-response generation; do streams require first-byte latency < 200ms?
- Model: you said you were evaluating a 13B open model variant - confirm exact family/version when you can.

Can you fill in the numbers below and attach any recent traffic logs? I attached a brief throughput_estimate.xlsx you can use to drop in values.

Requested fields:
- steady QPS:
- peak QPS (burst size and duration):
- average tokens/request:
- 95th percentile concurrency during peak:
- % of requests using streaming:

Next steps: once we have those numbers I'll run a preliminary tokens/sec and GPU sizing calc and loop in Marissa and Neha for kernel/runtime sizing and recommendations. If helpful we can do a 30-min technical session.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

messages_2_subject: Re: Finex: follow-up on throughput & latency SLOs
messages_2_body:
Thanks Rafael - good summary. Quick answers below and I attached a small sample of recent traffic logs (finex_sample_traffic_logs.txt).

- steady QPS: ~25 QPS (most business hours)
- peak QPS: spikes up to ~220 QPS for 8-12 minute bursts, ~10 times per day (usually after report runs)
- average tokens/request: ~350 tokens (range 150-1200)
- 95th percentile concurrency during peak: ~40 live sessions at peak
- % streaming: ~30% of requests use streaming (long-form content >500 tokens), streaming clients expect incrementally returned tokens; first-byte latency is important (p50 <200ms ideally)
- Model: evaluating 13B.op-v2 (open variant) - will confirm exact tag after I check with infra team.

Happy to join a technical call; we can do tomorrow between 11-12 PT.

Alex
Alex Thornton
Engineering Lead, Product Integrations
alex@finex.com

messages_3_subject: Re: Finex: follow-up on throughput & latency SLOs - preliminary sizing
messages_3_body:
Alex - thanks for the numbers, that's very helpful. I ran a quick back-of-envelope and attached a template + notes: redwood_throughput_sizing_template.xlsx and initial_sizing_notes.pdf. High-level takeaways: 

- Steady-state tokens/sec = steady QPS * avg tokens = 25 * 350 = ~8,750 tokens/sec.
- Peak tokens/sec (burst) = 220 * 350 = ~77,000 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent sessions implies we need to consider per-session KV cache and HTTP connection limits; if many sessions are mid-generation simultaneously, effective concurrency on the GPU could be higher for per-token scheduling.
- Streaming: since ~30% of requests are streamed and many of those are long (>500 tokens), we need to ensure first-token latency (p50/p95) meets your targets; continuous batching can help for throughput but may add a few ms of scheduling delay - we should benchmark with real samples.

Looking at those numbers, our next items:
1) Technical call (30 min) to validate: sequence lengths, model checkpoints, whether You use server-push streaming or chunked responses, and acceptable tail-latency tradeoffs.
2) I'll prepare a GPU instance recommendation + expected tokens/sec per instance based on the 13B.op-v2 variant and typical sequence lengths; Marissa/Neha will propose kernel/quantization options and an autoscaling policy draft.
3) If you can share a week of anonymized request traces (or the attached sample expanded) that'll let us compute realistic batching gains and cache hit rates.

Proposing a call tomorrow 2026-03-12 at 11:00 PT - does that work?

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_throughput_sizing_template.xlsx, initial_sizing_notes.pdf
messages_4_subject: Re: Finex: follow-up on throughput & latency SLOs - some clarifying Qs
messages_4_body:
Alex / Rafael - quick technical clarifications from our sizing team before the call: 

1) Streaming semantics: when you say streaming for long-form, is the client maintaining a single persistent HTTP/WS connection per session that expects token deltas, or are you using repeated short polling?
2) Peak burst shape: you noted 220 QPS for ~8-12 minutes - is the arrival distribution Poisson-like or more synchronized (e.g., many users at once)? Synchronized bursts reduce batching efficiency.
3) Tokenization: is your avg tokens/request measured pre-tokenizer or post-tokenizer? We need tokenizer-based token counts for accurate tokens/sec.
4) Retry behaviour: do clients retry aggressively on latency spikes? Retries can multiply effective QPS.

If you can answer any of the above in the meeting or via reply, that'll help us choose batching window and kernel configs.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

messages_5_subject: Re: Finex: follow-up on throughput & latency SLOs - answers to clarifications
messages_5_body:
Marissa / Rafael - quick answers ahead of tomorrow's call: 

1) Streaming: client uses persistent HTTP/WS connections for interactive sessions; tokens are pushed as generated (server-push).
2) Burst shape: fairly synchronized - typically an internal job triggers notifications that cause many users to poll/report within ~10 minutes. So arrival is spiky (lower batching efficiency).
3) Token counts: the numbers I gave are post-tokenizer (we measure with the same tokenizer as the model).
4) Retries: clients implement exponential backoff; we don't see aggressive immediate retries but failed requests are retried once within ~10s.

Confirming the 11:00 PT slot tomorrow works for our team - sending invites now.

Alex
